posts.central_knowledge_unit: Pierre de Coubertin: Visionary and Founder of the Modern Olympics
posts.claim: Pierre de Coubertin was a principal organizer of the 1894 Paris Congress that adopted the revival of the Olympic Games, established the International Olympic Committee, and set Athens as the site of the first IOC-era modern Olympic Games in 1896. He is therefore accurately described as a central founder of the IOC-era modern Olympic movement, but not as the sole originator of every modern Olympic revival idea or event.

posts.angle: Cultural continuity and accurate historical framing of a surviving indigenous sport
posts.central_knowledge_unit: Ulama, a 3,400-year-old ballgame that survived in Mexico | AP News
posts.claim: Ulama is a living traditional game in Sinaloa that Mexico’s cultural-heritage inventory identifies as a continuity of the pre-Hispanic Mesoamerican ballgame. In the hip (cadera) form, teams use a heavy natural-rubber ball and play it with the hip; the broader Mesoamerican ballgame tradition has archaeological and scholarly evidence reaching roughly 3,500 years into the past. It is therefore supportable to describe ulama as a modern continuation of an ancient Mesoamerican ballgame, but not to state as an established fact that the identical modern sport itself is exactly 3,400 years old or that it is definitively one of the oldest team sports.
posts.headline: Ulama: Ancient Mesoamerican Ballgame Lives On in Modern Mexico
